source.title: Residential green space and hair cortisol concentration in 2,940 adults: a cross-sectional study
source.abstract: Chronic stress is associated with cardiovascular and metabolic disease, and hair cortisol concentration provides a retrospective measure of cortisol exposure over roughly the preceding three months. We analysed data from 2,940 adults aged 25 to 74 in a population cohort in Flanders. Residential green space was quantified as the proportion of vegetated land cover within a 300-metre buffer of each participant's home address, derived from 10-metre resolution satellite imagery. Hair samples of 3 cm were collected from the posterior vertex. After adjustment for age, sex, household income, educational attainment, smoking, body mass index and season of sampling, a 10 percentage point increase in green space was associated with a 4.2% lower hair cortisol concentration (95% CI 1.8% to 6.5%). The association was stronger among participants in the lowest income tertile. Because the design is cross-sectional, we cannot establish the direction of the relationship, and residential self-selection may explain part of it. We did not investigate biological mechanisms.
source.tldr: Adults living in greener neighbourhoods had 4.2% lower hair cortisol per 10 percentage points of additional green space, in a cross-sectional analysis.
